Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
23-y-o woman with rapid upper-lip swelling, throat tightness, dyspnoea and dizziness within 30 min of eating prawn soup – high suspicion for IgE-mediated anaphylaxis; emergency services activated.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive swelling of left upper lip starting ~30 min after prawn soup (≈19:00 today); now enlarging, throbbing, “pumping,” with throat tightness, breathing difficulty and dizziness.  
• Associated symptoms: Possible chest tightness; denies other specifics (no urticaria or fever mentioned).  
• Pertinent negatives: No known trauma; no current antihistamine use; no ACE-inhibitor use.  
• Past medical history: Asthma; peanut allergy; prior severe food-related reaction age 6 requiring hospital; similar facial swelling + dyspnoea after Chinese meal 1 yr ago.  
• Medications: Salbutamol inhaler PRN; occasional unspecified oral antihistamines; no maintenance inhaler.  
• Allergies: Peanuts (IgE mediated). Suspected new shellfish (prawn) allergy.  
• Social / preventive: Lives with mother (present at call end); occasional alcohol; no other details.

Examination:
• Virtual video: Visible upper-lip swelling increasing during call; patient appears breathless and becomes dizzy.  
• No formal vitals obtained. No other system exam documented.

Impression:
Most likely: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis triggered by shellfish (prawn) – rapid onset after exposure, progressive orofacial swelling, airway symptoms, dizziness, atopic history.  
Alternate considerations:  
1. Isolated allergic angioedema without systemic involvement – less likely given respiratory compromise/dizziness.  
2. Hereditary angioedema – unlikely (clear food trigger, childhood peanut allergy).

Plan:
• Immediate management:  
  – Advised mother to administer available oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.  
  – Doctor contacted emergency services (999) for urgent transport to ED for suspected anaphylaxis ± intramuscular epinephrine and airway support.  
• Post-hospital: Patient to arrange follow-up with primary care/allergy clinic after discharge to review reaction, prescribe epinephrine auto-injectors, discuss avoidance of shellfish/peanut exposure, and consider formal allergy testing & action plan.

Quality checks
● Missing elements: Objective vitals, full medication/allergy list, past surgical/family history, vaccination status, formal follow-up appointment date.  
● Conflicts: None significant between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but lacks physical exam and vitals; minor background noise; otherwise coherent.
